facts.statement: The only known species of Luskhan is L. itilensis, which was first described in 2017.
facts.quote: The only known species is L. itilensis, first described in 2017 from a well-preserved and nearly complete skeleton discovered in the Ulyanovsk region.

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton of Luskhan was discovered in 2002 by Gleb N. Uspensky near Slantsevy Rudnik in the Ulyanovsk region of western Russia.
facts.quote: The holotype and only known specimen of Luskhan consists of an almost complete, three-dimensionally preserved pliosaur skeleton, discovered in 2002 by Russian paleontologist Gleb N. Uspensky on the eastern bank of the Volga River, about 3 km north of the village of Slantsevy Rudnik in the Ulyanovsk region of western Russia.

facts.statement: The species Luskhan itilensis was formally described in a paper published in Current Biology on June 5, 2017.
facts.quote: Uspensky co-authored a research paper describing YKM 68344/1_262 that was published in the journal Current Biology on June 5, 2017.

facts.statement: The genus name Luskhan combines Mongolian and Turkic words for water spirits with the suffix for 'chief'.
facts.quote: The genus name, Luskhan, is derived from luuses, water spirits and masters of water in Mongolian and Turkic mythology, combined with the suffix khan, meaning "chief".

facts.statement: The species name itilensis means 'of the Volga River', referencing the ancient Turkic name for the river.
facts.quote: Itil is the ancient Turkic name for the Volga River, hence the species epithet itilensis means "of the Volga River".

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Luskhan measures 6.5 meters in length.
facts.quote: The holotype of Luskhan measures 6.5 m long.

facts.statement: Luskhan had a lower jaw that was 1.59 meters long.
facts.quote: It has a lower jaw 1.59 m long.

facts.statement: Luskhan possessed 14 cervical vertebrae, a number intermediate between those of Pliosaurus and Brachauchenius.
facts.quote: The number of cervical vertebrae in Luskhan (14) can be seen as intermediate between Pliosaurus (18) and Brachauchenius (12).

facts.statement: Luskhan lacked typical brachauchenine hunting adaptations, including a very thin snout, no keel on the jaw symphysis, no gap in the tooth row, expanded upper jaw bones, and no canine-like teeth.
facts.quote: Unusually, Luskhan also lacks many of the adaptations for hunting large prey seen in other brachauchenines: the snout is very thin; there is no keel on the bottom of the fused symphysis of the lower jaw; there is no diastema (or gap in the tooth row); the bones of the upper jaw (the premaxilla and maxilla) are expanded outwards; and there are no caniniform ("canine-like") teeth.

facts.statement: The number of teeth in the premaxilla of Luskhan is ambiguous, with reports varying between six and seven.
facts.quote: The number of teeth in the premaxilla of the taxon is ambiguous, being reported as either six or seven.

facts.statement: Luskhan's front flipper bones (ulna and radius) were very small, roughly the same size as its hind flipper tarsus, with the ulna being longer.
facts.quote: The ulna and radius of the front flippers are very small, being only about the same size as the tarsus of the hind flippers; the former of these is longer.

facts.statement: Unlike other pliosaurids, Luskhan lacked an epipodial foramen where the ulna and radius met.
facts.quote: Unlike all other pliosaurids, there is no opening (epipodial foramen) where the two bones meet.

facts.statement: Luskhan is classified as an early-diverging brachauchenine, showing a mix of traits from both basal and derived pliosaurs.
facts.quote: As an early-diverging brachauchenine, Luskhan consequently exhibits an intermediate combination of traits seen in more basal (less specialized) and more derived (more specialized) pliosaurs.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses vary, but Luskhan is often considered the next most basal brachauchenine after Makhaira.
facts.quote: In the strict consensus of the 20,000 most parsimonious phylogenetic trees recovered, Makhaira forms a polytomy with Pliosaurus species, instead of forming a clade with other brachauchenines; however, in the consensus of the 24 most parsimonious trees, it is the most basal brachauchenine, with Luskhan being the next most basal brachauchenine.

facts.statement: Luskhan lived during the Lower Cretaceous period in western Russia.
facts.quote: Luskhan (meaning "water spirit chief") is an extinct genus of large pliosaurid plesiosaurs from the Lower Cretaceous of western Russia.

facts.statement: Luskhan convergently evolved traits similar to the distantly related polycotylids, despite their lineages diverging over 10 million years ago.
facts.quote: With these features, it is the pliosaur that approaches closest to the distantly-related piscivorous polycotylids, having convergently evolved these traits more than 10 million years apart.

facts.statement: There is a debate regarding whether including Stenorhynchosaurus in the Brachaucheninae clade requires redefining the group, with describers of Stenorhynchosaurus arguing for redefinition while the describers of Luskhan did not.
facts.quote: While María Páramo-Fonseca and colleagues, the describers of Stenorhynchosaurus, indicated that including it in the Brachaucheninae would necessitate a re-definition of the clade, Fischer and colleagues did not see this as necessary.

facts.statement: Luskhan is known from an almost complete fossilized skeleton found near the Volga River in European Russia.
facts.quote: Luskhan itilensis es conocido a partir de un esqueleto fosilizado casi completo encontrado cerca del río Volga en la Rusia europea.

facts.statement: The known skeleton of Luskhan measures 6.5 meters in length.
facts.quote: Este esqueleto mide 6.5 metros de longitud.

facts.statement: Luskhan had a relatively short neck leading to an elongated skull with a narrow snout and a jaw reaching 1.6 meters in length.
facts.quote: Al final de su cuello relativamente corto, surgía su cráneo alargado con un hocico estrecho, con una mandíbula que alcanzaba 1.6 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Luskhan possessed seven premaxillary teeth, with the first one being procumbent and nearly horizontal.
facts.quote: Siete dientes premaxilares, el primero de los cuales es procumbente y casi horizontal

facts.statement: The suture between the squamosal and quadrate bones expands posteriorly into a hook-shaped rugose process on the squamosal.
facts.quote: La sutura entre los huesos escamosal y cuadrado se expande posteriormente en un proceso rugoso en forma de gancho en el escamosal.

facts.statement: Ecological analysis suggests Luskhan likely preyed on small, soft-bodied animals.
facts.quote: Ecologically speaking, Luskhan probably preyed on small, soft animals.

facts.statement: The slender snout, long symphysis, and relatively short tooth row suggest Luskhan fed on soft prey.
facts.quote: This is suggested by the slender snout, the long symphysis, and the relatively short tooth row compared to other thalassophoneans.

facts.statement: Its narrow face, long mandibular symphysis, and smaller isodont teeth imply a diet of soft-bodied prey like fish and squid rather than large prey.
facts.quote: Este rasgo, junto con una larga sínfisis mandibular, y la presencia de dientes isodontos más pequeños, implican que tenía una dieta de presas de cuerpo blando tales como peces y calamares, en lugar de las presas más grandes consumidas por otros talasofoneos.

facts.statement: Luskhan independently evolved to occupy a lower trophic level 10 million years after polycotylids did.
facts.quote: Thus, Luskhan departed from the typical apex predator niche of thalassophoneans in order to colonize a lower trophic level, having done so independently 10 million years after polycotylids.

facts.statement: Luskhan lived during the upper Hauterivian epoch of the early Cretaceous, approximately 128 million years ago.
facts.quote: Magnetostratigraphy indicates that this zone dates to the upper Hauterivian epoch of the early Cretaceous Period, approximately 128 million years ago.

facts.statement: The time range for Luskhan is the Hauterivian, between 132.6 and 125.77 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hauterivian to Hauterivian (132.6 to 125.77 million years ago)

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, cataloged as YKM 68344/1_262, was discovered by Gleb N. Uspensky.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo, catalogado como YKM 68344/1_262, fue hallado por Gleb N. Uspensky.

facts.statement: The genus name Luskhan is derived from 'luus,' a water spirit and master in Turkic and Mongolian legends, and 'khan,' meaning chief.
facts.quote: El nombre del género, Luskhan proviene de luus, un espíritu y amo del agua de las leyendas turcas y mongoles, y khan, que significa jefe.

facts.statement: The species name itilensis means 'of the Volga,' derived from the ancient Turkic name for the Volga River.
facts.quote: Itil es el nombre antiguo turco para el río Volga, del que proviene el nombre de la especie itilensis, que significa "del Volga".

facts.statement: The genus Luskhan was described by Fischer et al. in 2017.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Fischer et al. 2017

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Luskhan is Luskhan itilensis.
facts.quote: type_species: Luskhan itilensis

facts.statement: Luskhan is classified within the subfamily Brachaucheninae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Brachaucheninae

facts.statement: Luskhan belongs to the family Pliosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Pliosauridae

facts.statement: Analyses show Luskhan is the most polycotylid-like pliosaurid based on skull traits, though its body plan differs.
facts.quote: Principal component and ecomorphological analyses place Luskhan as being significantly closer to polycotylids than other thalassophoneans in terms of skull traits, but not in terms of the rest of the body; thus, Luskhan is the most polycotylid-like pliosaurid.

facts.statement: While Luskhan's skull and teeth resemble polycotylids, its axial skeleton and flippers remain like other thalassophonean pliosaurids.
facts.quote: Aunque el parecido con los policotílidos se extiende al cráneo y dientes, el esqueleto axial y las aletas siguen siendo como las de otros pliosáuridos talasofoneos.

facts.statement: It is debated whether serrations and weakly trihedral teeth in Luskhan are functional or vestigial traits retained from ancestors.
facts.quote: A few traits in Luskhan are shared with typical thalassophoneans, such as the presence of serrations in the rearmost teeth and the presence of weakly trihedral (triangular in cross-section) teeth; however, these are probably vestigial traits retained from Pliosaurus-like ancestors.
